title: os migrate apply on an empty database writes no organization-ownership birth marker, so the fresh install's first os serve is refused as a 17.x / 18.0 pre-release database
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect with a named location and a reproduction.

- Category: ① (reach: public entry point measured once with a wrong result — `os migrate apply` then `os serve`, the CLI doors an operator's deploy script runs).
- Who acts: the seat that owns the 18.x organization-ownership line (follow-up to PR #24681, steps 5 and 6) — `packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts` and `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`.
- Dedup: local scan of the 625 newest issues (state=all, open and closed) for `birth|ownership|ceremony` — 25 hits, and for `migrate apply` — 5 hits; none describes this (closest: #24566, #23684, #23848 — different defects, all closed). Also read #24581 / #24582 (the step 5 / step 6 cards PR #24681 closed).

reach: `os migrate apply --yes` then `os serve`, measured twice on an empty SQLite file at 307ce4c4.
Path: platform-core.v18-boot-refusals
QA-source: #24838 · platform-core.v18-boot-refusals · observed beside the clauses
Checklist item priority: P0
type: Bug

## What happens

PR #24681's body states the contract: "Every CLI boot writes the birth half too. This is `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerPlugin` in `createStandaloneStack`. It never refuses. Without it, an install whose first command is `os migrate apply` or `os seed` would be refused by its first `os serve`." For `os migrate apply` it does not hold.

## Reproduction (framework 307ce4c4, examples/app-showcase, reproduced twice on fresh files)

1. From `examples/app-showcase`: `os migrate apply --yes --database-url file:/tmp/RUN/mig.db` (the file does not exist yet). Exit 0; the log prints `Created/extended 71 table(s)`.
2. Read the ledger: `SELECT count(*) FROM sys_migration` answers 0 — no `adr-0131-organization-ownership` row.
3. `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:/tmp/RUN/mig.db OS_AUTH_SECRET=... OS_SECRET_KEY=(64 hex) os serve -p PORT`.
   - Expected: the server starts (this release created the database).
   - Actual: exit 1, never listening, printing: "This database carries no organization-ownership marker: 17.x or an 18.0 pre-release (18.0.0-next.*) created it, and this release serves only a database it created itself or one its ownership ceremony upgraded. … Run 'os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN' …".
4. Control: the same `os serve` over a never-touched file logs `[organization-ownership] a datastore created from empty: birth marker written (shape generation 1, …)` and starts.

Side effects seen on the same database:
- `os dev` over it is refused the same way, then auto-runs the ceremony and prints "This development database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape — upgrading it in place", about a database HEAD created minutes earlier.
- The way out works: `os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`, then `--apply --plan-file PLAN --backup-taken` → complete true, blocking 0, and `os serve` starts. But an operator who just created a fresh 18.x database is told it came from 17.x and is sent through an upgrade ceremony.

## Mechanism (verified independently from code, RUNNER rule 7)

- `os migrate apply` boots with `deferSchemaDdl: true` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts` ~213-216), which arms `com.objectstack.cli.defer-schema-ddl` (`packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts`).
- In the SQL driver's schema sync, a deferred object is stored and skipped before it is counted (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` ~12518-12540), so `getSchemaSyncStats()` answers `created: 0, existing: 0`.
- `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerPlugin.start()` → `recordOrganizationOwnershipBirth` → `ledgerStoreCreatedFromEmpty` answers false, and no marker is written.
- The tables are created later, at `stack.flushSchemaDdl()` (`apply.ts` ~632). Nothing calls `recordOrganizationOwnershipBirth` after the flush.
- The guard's own docblock (around lines 369-371) treats "deferred boots report nothing created" as covering only the ceremony's boots. `os migrate apply` is also a deferred boot.
- `os migrate plan` first is harmless: it never flushes, so the file stays empty and the first `os serve` writes the marker. There is no `os seed` command in this CLI (`os seed --help` → command not found), so the PR body's second example cannot be exercised.

## Why it matters

Running `os migrate apply` before `os serve` is a normal deploy-script order. Under this release that order turns a fresh install into one the boot guard calls a 17.x or 18.0 pre-release database, and the refusal text says so. The pins for the birth half (`organization-ownership-boot-guard.test.ts`, `organization-ownership-boot-guard.kernel.test.ts`) exercise boots with schema sync, so none of them covers a deferred-DDL boot followed by a flush.
